core_obligations: Build a constructible graded sheaf (proof lines 5741-5760): set R equal to the direct sum of the quotients I^n/I^{n+1}, a Noetherian ring; since each F/I^n F is constructible over Lambda/I^n, the graded pieces I^n F / I^{n+1} F are constructible over Lambda/I and hence pullbacks of constructible etale sheaves G_n; the direct sum G is a sheaf of R-modules and the natural map G_0 tensor over Lambda/I with the constant sheaf on R is surjective onto G because each multiplication map on the graded pieces is surjective.

Find a partition making G locally constant (proof lines 5760-5768): by the constructibility proposition for sheaves of modules over a Noetherian ring, G is a constructible sheaf of R-modules, so there is a finite partition X = the disjoint union of the X_i by locally closed subschemes such that each G|_{X_i} is locally constant of finite type.

Descend to F (proof lines 5768-5778): replacing X by X_i one may assume G locally constant, hence each successive quotient I^n F/I^{n+1} F is locally constant; the short exact sequences 0 -> I^n F/I^{n+1} F -> F/I^{n+1} F -> F/I^n F -> 0 together with the local constancy of the kernels of surjections of locally constant finite type sheaves give, by induction on n, that each F/I^n F is locally constant of finite type, and the same short exact sequences with the kernel argument give that F itself is lisse on X_i.
proof_roadmap: Form the associated graded sheaf of the ideal-adic filtration and show it is a constructible sheaf of finite type over the Noetherian graded ring.
Use the partition theorem to make the graded sheaf locally constant.
Propagate local constancy back to the successive quotients and then to the sheaf itself by induction along the short exact sequences.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a Noetherian scheme X, a Noetherian ring Lambda and an ideal I, every constructible Lambda-sheaf on the pro-etale site of X becomes lisse on the pieces of a finite partition by locally closed subschemes (statement lines 5731-5739). The proof (proof lines 5741-5780) builds the associated graded sheaf of the ideal-adic filtration as a constructible sheaf of finite type over a Noetherian graded ring, makes it locally constant by the partition theorem, and propagates local constancy back to the sheaf by induction along the short exact sequences. H3: an original construction reducing a pro-etale statement to a graded etale one, written out in full.
